Non-Hermitian strongly interacting Dirac fermions: a quantum Monte-Carlo study

Xue-Jia Yu International Center for Quantum Materials, School of Physics, Peking University, Beijing 100871, China    Zhiming Pan Institute for Theoretical Sciences, WestLake University, Hangzhou 310024, China    Limei Xu International Center for Quantum Materials, School of Physics, Peking University, Beijing 100871, China Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter, Beijing, China Interdisciplinary Institute of Light-Element Quantum Materials and Research Center for Light-Element Advanced Materials, Peking University, Beijing, China    Zi-Xiang Li zixiangli@iphy.ac.cn Beijing National Laboratory for Condensed Matter Physics, and Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China School of Physical Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, China
Abstract

Exotic quantum phases and phase transition in the strongly interacting Dirac systems has attracted tremendous interests. On the other hand, non-Hermitian physics, usually associated with dissipation arising from the coupling to environment, emerges as a frontier of modern physics in recent years. In this letter, we investigate the interplay between non-Hermitian physics and strong correlation in Dirac-fermion systems. We develop a sign-problem-free projector quantum Monte-Carlo (QMC) algorithm for the non-Hermitian interacting fermionic systems. Employing state-of-the-art projector QMC simulation, we decipher the ground-state phase diagram of the Honeycomb Hubbard model in the presence non-Hermitian asymmetric spin resolved hopping processes. Intriguingly, the antiferromagnetic ordering induced by Hubbard interaction is enhanced by the non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping. More remarkably, our study reveals that critical properties of the quantum phase transition between Dirac semi-metal and AF ordered phases are consistent with the XY universality class in Hermitian system, implying Hermiticity is emergent at the quantum critical point. The numerically-exact QMC approach utilized in this study is easily applied to other non-Hermitian interacting fermionic models, hence paving a new avenue to investigating quantum many-body physics in non-Hermitian systems.

Introduction.—Fathoming various exotic quantum phases and phase transition triggered by strong correlation between electrons is one of the central issues in modern condensed matter physics Sachdev (2011). In particular, inspired by the experimental realization of grapheneCastro Neto et al. (2009) and topological phasesQi and Zhang (2011); Hasan and Kane (2010), the interaction driving spontaneously symmetry breaking(SSB) phases and the associated quantum phase transition in Dirac fermions attracts growing interests. Since most strongly correlated systems are theoretically intractable in more than one-dimension, numerical approaches play vital roles in understanding Dirac-fermion systems in the presence of strong electronic interaction. Extensive numerical studies on interacting Dirac systems reveal an abundance of intriguing phenomena arising from the interplay between Dirac physics and strong electronic interaction, including interaction driven topological and other exotic phases of matterLang et al. (2013); Zheng et al. (2011); Hohenadler et al. (2011); Raghu et al. (2008); Scherer et al. (2015); Ghaemi et al. (2012); Roy and Herbut (2013); Weeks and Franz (2010); Li and Yao (2017), Gross-Neveu quantum criticalitySorella et al. (2012); Li et al. (2015a); Wang et al. (2014); Jian and Yao (2017); Herbut (2006); Tang et al. (2018); Sato et al. (2017); Scherer and Herbut (2016); Parisen Toldin et al. (2015); Roy et al. (2014); Assaad and Herbut (2013); He and Lu (2012); Tabatabaei et al. (2022); Lang and Läuchli (2019); Li et al. (2018); Yu et al. (2022) and continuous phase transition beyond Landau’s paradigm Li et al. (2017a, 2019, 2020); Da Liao et al. (2022).

In recent years, understanding non-Hermitian (NH) physics in quantum systems emerges as a frontier invoking considerable attention Ashida et al. (2020); Bender (2007); Lee and Chan (2014). Non-Hermitian physics arises if the system is coupled to the environment in the presence of dissipation or measurement Daley (2014); Dalibard et al. (1992); El-Ganainy et al. (2018); Ozawa et al. (2019). Additionally, non-Hermitian band Hamiltonian provides a conceptually effective description of the quasi-particle with finite life-time resulting from electron-electron/electron-phonon interaction or disorder scatteringShen and Fu (2018); Nagai et al. (2020). Previous studies demonstrate that plentiful exotic phenomena arise from non-Hermiticity, for instance skin effectYao and Wang (2018); Zhang et al. (2020); Song et al. (2019); Kunst et al. (2018); Jiang et al. (2019); Xiao et al. (2020); Yang et al. (2020); Zhang et al. (2022); Zhou et al. (2022); Wang et al. (2022), exotic topological phases Bergholtz et al. (2021); Xiao et al. (2017); Zhou et al. (2018); Zeuner et al. (2015); Ghatak and Das (2018); Zhou and Lee (2019); Kawabata et al. (2019a, b); Gong et al. (2018); Kawabata et al. (2018); Yao et al. (2018); Shen et al. (2018); Xue et al. (2020); Kawabata et al. (2019a); Zhou and Lee (2019); Ghatak and Das (2019); Lee et al. (2019); Okuma et al. (2020); Liu et al. (2022); Chen and Zhai (2018) and novel quantum critical behaviours Ashida et al. (2016, 2017); Kawabata et al. (2017); Yamamoto et al. (2022); Hayata et al. (2021); Pakrouski et al. (2021); Hamazaki et al. (2019); Alsallom et al. (2021); Pan et al. (2020); Jian et al. (2021a, b); He et al. (2022); Ortega-Taberner and Hermanns (2022); Hsieh and Chang (2022); Chang et al. (2020), which have not been established in Hermitian systems. Most early studies on non-Hermitian physics focus on single-particle systems, whereas very recently, increasing attentions have been paid in the quantum many-body effect in the non-Hermitian systems Yamamoto et al. (2019); Nakagawa et al. (2018); Lourenço et al. (2018); Yoshida et al. (2018); Orito and Imura (2022a); García-García et al. (2022); Wang et al. (2022a); Žnidarič (2022); Suthar et al. (2022); Chen et al. (2022a); Kawabata et al. (2022); García-García et al. (2022); Orito and Imura (2022b); Zhang et al. (2021); Tsubota et al. (2022); Hyart and Lado (2022); Sun et al. (2022); Zhai et al. (2020); Shackleton and Scheurer (2020); Takasu et al. (2020); Matsumoto et al. (2020); Tu et al. (2022a, b); Mák et al. (2023); Chen et al. (2022b); Wang et al. (2022b); Tzeng et al. (2021); Kattel et al. (2022); Han et al. (2023).

Nevertheless, the effects of interplay between strong correlation and Dirac fermions in non-Hermitian systems remain unexplored hitherto. Moreover, the intrinsically unbiased numerical algorithm applying to the non-Hermitian quantum many-body models in more than one-dimension is lacking. To address these crucial issues, we systematically study the ground-state properties of a non-Hermitian model featuring Dirac fermions in the presence of Hubbard interaction. For the first time, we develop a non-Hermitian version of projector QMC, applying to investigating the ground-state properties of non-Hermitian interacting fermionic systems. Remarkably, in the framework of the developed algorithm, we construct a non-Hermitian Hubbard model free from the notorious sign problem by virtue of time reversal symmetryWu and Zhang (2005); Li et al. (2017b, 2015b); Wang et al. (2015); Wei et al. (2016); Li and Yao (2019), enabling the large-scale QMC simulation without numerical approximation. Employing the numerically exact QMC simulation, we access the ground-state phase diagram of the model. The main results of the state-of-the-art QMC simulation are summarized as follows: 1. The interaction induced AFM order in Honeycomb Hubbard model is robust in the presence of non-Hermiticity. Intriguingly, the AFM order is enhanced by the asymmetric non-Hermitian process. 2. The numerical results reveal a continuous quantum phase transition occurring from DSM to AFM ordered phase. Surprisingly, despite the presence of non-Hermitician terms in the Hamiltonian, the quantum phase transition between Dirac semimetal (DSM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) phases belongs to the Hermitian version of chiral-XY universality classOstmeyer et al. (2020); Li et al. (2017a); Otsuka et al. (2018). Hence, the QMC results reveal the emergence of Hermiticity at the quantum phase transition point. Additionally, we present a systematic renormalization-group (RG) field theory analysis of the effective low-energy theory describing the non-Hermitian DSM-AFM transition, providing an understanding of the numerical results unveiled by QMC simulation. Notably, the QMC approach developed for non-Hermitian system is a general algorithm to tackle the non-Hermitian interacting fermionic models. We believe that our study paves a new route to investigating the quantum many-body physics in non-Hermitian systems.

Model and methods.—In this paper, we study the non-Hermitian extension of an interacting model on the honeycomb latticeSachdev (2011). Specifically, as shown in Fig.1 (a), we introduce the asymmetric hopping to construct a non-Hermitian version of the Hubbard modelHayata and Yamamoto (2021):

For δ=0𝛿0\delta=0, Eq LABEL:E1 is reduced to Hermitian Hubbard model on the honeycomb lattice, and has been extensively studiedSorella et al. (2012); Parisen Toldin et al. (2015). For Hamiltonian Eq. (LABEL:E1), in the non-interacting limit U=0𝑈0U=0 the eigenstates preserve 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT}-symmetry if δ𝛿\delta is smaller than the exceptional point (EP) δc=1subscript𝛿𝑐1\delta_{c}=1, at which eigenstates of the Hamiltonian coalesce. In the presence of Hubbard interaction, the exact diagonalization calculations in small clusters suggest the EP δc=1subscript𝛿𝑐1\delta_{c}=1 is stable under interaction, namely when δ<δc𝛿subscript𝛿𝑐\delta<\delta_{c} the eigenvalues of the interaction Hamiltonian Eq. (LABEL:E1) are real (see Sec.IV in Supplementary Materials (SM) for the details).

To investigate the ground-state properties of the non-Hermitian model, we generalize the algorithm of PQMC. To our knowledge, it is the first approximation-free quantum Monte-Carlo algorithm to study the ground-state properties of quantum many-body non-Hermitian model. Intriguingly, even though in the presence of non-Hermiticity, the model at half filling is free from the notorious sign problem at half filling in the framework of our algorithm, with the details introduced in SM I. Thus, the model offers a promising platform to investigate the interplay between non-Hermiticity and quantum many-body effects. In this work, we perform state-of-the-art QMC simulationsBlankenbecler et al. (1981); Scalapino and Sugar (1981); Li and Yao (2019) to study the ground-state phase diagram of the model. We focus on the model at half filling, and explore the quantum phase and the critical properties of the interaction driven quantum phase transition in non-Hermitian system.

Quantum phase diagram.—Before presenting the details of PQMC results, we briefly summarize the most salient features of the ground-state phase diagram of the model LABEL:E1. The schematic phase diagram with varying asymmetric hopping amplitude δ𝛿\delta and on-site Hubbard interaction U𝑈U is shown in Fig.1(b). For δ=0𝛿0\delta=0, a quantum phase transition from DSM to AFM phase is driven by the Hubbard interaction. We obtain critical point Uc=3.87subscript𝑈𝑐3.87U_{c}=3.87, which is consistent with previous studies in the literatureSorella et al. (2012). Our large-scale QMC simulations convincingly show that AFM order is robust, and more appealingly, strongly enhanced in the presence of non-Hermiticity. The transition point Ucsubscript𝑈𝑐U_{c} from DSM to the non-hermitian enhanced antiferromagnetic (NHEAFM) phase is shifted to a smaller value with increasing asymmetric hopping amplitude. The enhancement of AFM ordering by non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping is beyond our conventional understanding that non-Hermiticity is expected to destroy long-range ordering, and constitute a main discovery of our numerical simulation. Furthermore, we employ standard finite-size scaling (FSS) procedure to extract the critical exponents and determine universality class of the DSM-NHEAFM transition. Even though the lattice model is non-Hermitian, the results reveal that the transition between DSM and NHEAFM belongs to Hermitian chiral XY universality class Ostmeyer et al. (2020); Li et al. (2017a); Otsuka et al. (2018), implying Hermiticity is emergent at the DSM-NHEAFM transition point at low-energy limit.

Non-Hermitian enhanced antiferromagnetism—To investigate the effect of non-Hermiticity on AFM long-range ordering triggered by Hubbard interaction, we compute structure factor of AFM order, the definition of which is introduced in the section I of SM. Notice that non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping reduces the spin rotational S​U​(2)𝑆𝑈2SU(2) symmetry down to a U​(1)𝑈1U(1) corresponding to spin rotation in the x−y𝑥𝑦x-y plane, leading to the consequence that AFM structure factor in z𝑧z-direction SA​Fzsuperscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑧S_{AF}^{z} is not equivalent to that in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane SA​Fx​ysuperscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑥𝑦S_{AF}^{xy}. The numerical results unequivocally point out, AFM order in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane is dominant over the ordering in z𝑧z-direction in the presence of non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping, as shown in the section IV of SM. Hence, in the following we present the numerical results of AFM ordering in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane.

For the Hermitian limit δ=0𝛿0\delta=0, the standard FSS procedure yields the critical point of DSM-AFM transition Uc=3.87subscript𝑈𝑐3.87U_{c}=3.87, in agreement with extensive studies in previous literature. In the presence of non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping, the FSS analysis also establishes existence of AFM long-range ordering triggered by strong Hubbard interaction. Fig. 2(a)-(c) depicts the AFM structure factors SA​Fx​ysuperscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑥𝑦S_{AF}^{xy} for various interaction parameters and linear system sizes L𝐿L, at several non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping parameters δ=0.2,0.4,0.6𝛿0.20.40.6\delta=0.2,0.4,0.6, clearly indicating quantum phase transition occurs from a DSM to NHEAFM ordered phase with increasing Hubbard interaction strength. More remarkably, the critical value of Hubbard U𝑈U for the DSM-NHEAFM transition decreases upon increasing non-Hermitian hopping parameter δ𝛿\delta, suggesting the enhancement of AFM ordering by non-Hermiticity.

To explicitly observe the enhancement of AFM long-range order at thermodynamic limit, we present the AFM structure factor as a function of δ𝛿\delta for different linear system sizes L𝐿L and the extrapolated results to L→∞→𝐿L\rightarrow\infty ( Fig. 2(d)). The Hubbard interaction parameter is fixed at U=3.6𝑈3.6U=3.6. Fig. 2(d) clearly indicates AFM structure factors monotonically increases with δ𝛿\delta. For U=3.6𝑈3.6U=3.6, the ground state is DSM with non-Hermitian hopping δ=0𝛿0\delta=0, which is verified by the extrapolated result of AFM structure factor SA​Fx​y​(L→∞)=0superscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑥𝑦→𝐿0S_{AF}^{xy}(L\rightarrow\infty)=0. With increasing δ𝛿\delta, the AFM ordering is enhanced, resulting in a quantum phase transition from DSM to AFM ordred phase driven by non-Hermitian hopping, occurring at δc≈0.4subscript𝛿𝑐0.4\delta_{c}\approx 0.4. Consequently, the numerical results unambiguously demonstrate the enhancement of AFM ordering by non-Hermiticity in model Eq. (LABEL:E1).

To determine accurate transition point between DSM and AFM ordered phases, we compute the RG-invariant correlation-length ratio for AFM order defined as:

R​(L)A​FX​Y=SA​FX​Y​(Q→,L)SA​FX​Y​(Q→−δ​q→)−1,𝑅superscriptsubscript𝐿𝐴𝐹𝑋𝑌superscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑋𝑌→𝑄𝐿superscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑋𝑌→𝑄𝛿→𝑞1R(L)_{AF}^{XY}=\frac{S_{AF}^{XY}(\vec{Q},L)}{S_{AF}^{XY}(\vec{Q}-\delta\vec{q})}-1, (2)

where Q→=(0,0)→𝑄00\vec{Q}=(0,0) labels the momentum at which the structure factor is maximum for AFM order. δ​q→=(2​πL,2​πL)𝛿→𝑞2𝜋𝐿2𝜋𝐿\delta\vec{q}=(\frac{2\pi}{L},\frac{2\pi}{L}) is a minimal momentum on lattice shift from Q→→𝑄\vec{Q}. In the long-range ordered phase, correlation length ratio increases with system size, while if the AFM order is short-ranged, the trend is opposite. At the critical point, the RG-invariant correlation-length ratio is independent on system size owing to the nature of scaling invariant, therefore offering a powerful theoretical approach to identify critical point of phase transition. In Fig. 3, we present the results of correlation-length ratios as a function of Hubbard U𝑈U for several values of δ𝛿\delta, giving rise to the DSM-NHEAFM quantum critical points, which are approximately consistent with the results given by the finite-size scaling of AFM structure factors. Consequently, we obtain the ground-state phase diagram of Hubbard model on Honeycomb lattice in the presence of non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping, explicitly revealing the AFM ordering associated with electronic interaction is strongly enhanced by the non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping in Eq. (LABEL:E1).

Emergent chiral XY universality class.—Having accessing the ground-state phase diagram of the non-Hermitian model Eq. (LABEL:E1), we investigate the critical property of the quantum phase transition between DSM and NHEAFM phases. In the absence of non-Hermitian hopping, DSM-AFM transition featured in Hubbard model on Honeycomb lattice is extensively investigated, belonging to chiral-Heisenberg universality class Ladovrechis et al. (2023). As aforementioned, the non-Hermitian hopping introduced in Eq. (LABEL:E1) breaks the spin S​U​(2)𝑆𝑈2SU(2) symmetry to U​(1)𝑈1U(1), is thus expected to change the universality class of the phase transition. In Hermitian system, the continuous quantum phase transition between DSM and the in-plane AFM ordered phase breaking U​(1)𝑈1U(1) symmetry is described by the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model, and belongs to chiral-XY universality class, as revealed by field-theory analysis and numerical simulation on lattice models. In this section, we decipher the critical properties of the DSM-AFM transition in the presence non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping process.

In the regime sufficiently close to critical point Ucsubscript𝑈𝑐U_{c}, the AFM structure factors obeys the scaling relation:

Other critical exponents are available to deduce from η𝜂\eta and ν𝜈\nu by hyper-scaling relation. The results of RA​FX​Ysuperscriptsubscript𝑅𝐴𝐹𝑋𝑌R_{AF}^{XY} for different system sizes exhibit excellent collapse, ensuring our analysis yields convincing results of critical exponents. Furthermore, with the choice of a different value of δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6, we implement the same procedure and extract critical exponents for the DSM-NHAFM transition. The results are included in the section V of SM, in agreement with the results for δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4.

To conclude, the non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping introduced in model Eq. (LABEL:E1) breaks S​U​(2)𝑆𝑈2SU(2) spin rotational symmetry to U​(1)𝑈1U(1), favoring AFM ordering in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane. Intriguingly, although in the presence of non-Hermiticity, DSM-NHEAFM transition realized in the model belongs to the same universality class as the Hermitian version of the phase transition, namely chiral-XY universality class.

Low-energy effective theory.—We derive the effective Hamiltonian describing the low-energy Dirac fermions in the non-Hermitian model Eq. (LABEL:E1) on honeycomb lattice (see Sec.VI in SM for the details). The result writes:

h​(q→)=−vF​(qx​s0⊗σ1+qy​s0⊗σ2−i​qy​δt​s3⊗σ1−i​qx​δt​s3⊗σ2),ℎ→𝑞subscript𝑣𝐹tensor-productsubscript𝑞𝑥subscript𝑠0subscript𝜎1tensor-productsubscript𝑞𝑦subscript𝑠0subscript𝜎2tensor-product𝑖subscript𝑞𝑦𝛿𝑡subscript𝑠3subscript𝜎1tensor-product𝑖subscript𝑞𝑥𝛿𝑡subscript𝑠3subscript𝜎2h(\vec{q})=-v_{F}(q_{x}s_{0}\otimes\sigma_{1}+q_{y}s_{0}\otimes\sigma_{2}-\frac{iq_{y}\delta}{t}s_{3}\otimes\sigma_{1}-\frac{iq_{x}\delta}{t}s_{3}\otimes\sigma_{2}), (4)

where s,σ𝑠𝜎s,\sigma are Pauli matrices acting on spin and sublattice spaces respectively, and vF=3​t2subscript𝑣𝐹3𝑡2v_{F}=\frac{3t}{2} is the Fermi velocity in the absence of non-Hermitian hopping, namely δ=0𝛿0\delta=0. The direct diagonalization of the Hamiltonian yields the energy dispersion (see Sec.VI in SM), which is purely real and corresponds to a Dirac cone with renormalized Fermi velocity v~F=vF​1−(δ/t)2subscript~𝑣𝐹subscript𝑣𝐹1superscript𝛿𝑡2\tilde{v}_{F}=v_{F}\sqrt{1-(\delta/t)^{2}}. Since the density of state(DOS) near the energy of Dirac point is proportional to the inverse of Fermi velocity, the reduction of Fermi velocity results in the increase of DOS near the Dirac point, which offers a plausible explanation on the enhancement of AFM order as revealed by our numerical simulation. More crucially, to understand the emergence of Hermiticity at XY-AFM QCP as unambiguously revealed in our numerical results, we perform an one-loop perturbative renormalization group calculation on the Gross-Neveu low-energy effective theory (see the SM VII for details ). The beta function of the non-Hermitian parameter δ𝛿\delta is d​δd​l=−2​g^2​δ𝑑𝛿𝑑𝑙2superscript^𝑔2𝛿\frac{d\delta}{dl}=-2\hat{g}^{2}\delta (see the SM VII for details), demonstrating the irrelevance of the non-Hermitian parameter at low-energy limit. Therefore, the Hermitian chiral XY universal class is emergent at the QCP. We leave a more systematic field-theory study as a future work.

Conclusion and discussion.—In summary, we propose an innovative QMC algorithm to investigate the ground-state properties of quantum many-body models in the presence of non-Hermiticity. We construct a non-Hermitian interacting fermionic model, more explicitly, Hubbard model with non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping. Remarkably, the model is free from the notorious sign problem, such that the ground-state properties of model with large system size are accessible. Employing state-of-the-art QMC simulation, we systematic investigate the quantum phases and phase transition emerging in this model. The results unambiguously reveal that the AFM ordering triggered by strong Hubbard interaction is enhanced by non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping. The interaction driven quantum phase transition from DSM to the NHEAFM phase belongs to the chiral-XY universality class as previously unveiled in Hermitian systems, although the non-Hermiticity is present in the model.

In the perspective of experimental realization, the non-Hermitian hopping process is induced by the single-particle loss or gain on the bond associated with coupling to the environment, corresponding to Lindblad operator L⟨i​j⟩=ci+cjsubscript𝐿delimited-⟨⟩𝑖𝑗subscript𝑐𝑖subscript𝑐𝑗L_{\left\langle ij\right\rangle}=c_{i}+c_{j} in the quantum master equation. When the quantum-jump terms are neglible, the resulting effective Hamiltonian involves the non-Hermitian hopping terms as discussed in our study. More remarkably, since the principles to guarantee sign-problem-free in QMC simulation proposed in Hermitian models are straightforwardly generalized to non-Hermitian algorithm, it is promising to design more non-Hermitian interacting fermionic models featuring fascinating physics based on our approach. For example, designing sign-problem-free models and investigating the interacting effect on the non-Hermitian topological phase is particularly intriguing. Hence, our study paves a new avenue towards understanding the interplay between quantum many-body and non-Hermitian physics in a theoretically controlled approach.

I Supplemental Material for Phase Diagram of Non-Hermitian Interacting Dirac Fermion

I.1 Section I: Projector Quantum Monte-Carlo algorithm for non-Hermitian fermionic model

For QMC simulation on fermionic quantum many-body systems, projector QMC is a widely used algorithm to investigate the ground-state properties of the models. The conventional version of projector QMC algorithm is constraint for the Hermitian many-body models. We develop a generalized projector QMC algorithm to simulate the ground-state properties of the non-Hermitian interacting fermionic models. For non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, the eigenvalues are not guaranteed to be real. The observables associated with the ground state of a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian are evaluated as:

⟨O⟩G=⟨ψL,G|O^|ψR,G⟩⟨ψL,G|ψR,G⟩subscriptdelimited-⟨⟩𝑂𝐺quantum-operator-productsubscript𝜓𝐿𝐺^𝑂subscript𝜓𝑅𝐺inner-productsubscript𝜓𝐿𝐺subscript𝜓𝑅𝐺\displaystyle\left\langle O\right\rangle_{G}=\frac{\langle\psi_{L,G}|\hat{O}|\psi_{R,G}\rangle}{\langle\psi_{L,G}|\psi_{R,G}\rangle} (5)

In the scheme of projector QMC simulation, the ground state of an interacting Hamiltonian is achieved through projecting a trivial wave function. As long as the trivial wave function is not orthogonal to the ground-state wave function ⟨ψT|ψG⟩≠0inner-productsubscript𝜓𝑇subscript𝜓𝐺0\langle\psi_{T}|\psi_{G}\rangle\neq 0, which is generically obeyed in quantum many-body systems, the ground state of a given Hamiltonian is accessed at sufficiently large projector parameter: |ψG⟩=limΘ→∞e−Θ​H^​|ψT⟩ketsubscript𝜓𝐺subscript→Θsuperscript𝑒Θ^𝐻ketsubscript𝜓𝑇|\psi_{G}\rangle=\lim_{\Theta\rightarrow\infty}e^{-\Theta\hat{H}}|\psi_{T}\rangle. Correspondingly, in the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, the right and left ground states are accessed as: |ψR,G⟩=limΘ→∞e−Θ​H^​|ψR,T⟩ketsubscript𝜓𝑅𝐺subscript→Θsuperscript𝑒Θ^𝐻ketsubscript𝜓𝑅𝑇|\psi_{R,G}\rangle=\lim_{\Theta\rightarrow\infty}e^{-\Theta\hat{H}}|\psi_{R,T}\rangle and |ψL,G⟩=limΘ→∞e−Θ​H^†​|ψL,T⟩ketsubscript𝜓𝐿𝐺subscript→Θsuperscript𝑒Θsuperscript^𝐻†ketsubscript𝜓𝐿𝑇|\psi_{L,G}\rangle=\lim_{\Theta\rightarrow\infty}e^{-\Theta\hat{H}^{\dagger}}|\psi_{L,T}\rangle, where |ψR,T⟩ketsubscript𝜓𝑅𝑇|\psi_{R,T}\rangle and |ψL,T⟩ketsubscript𝜓𝐿𝑇|\psi_{L,T}\rangle are right and left trial wave function. Thus, the expectation value of ground state for non-Hermitian Hamiltonian are evaluated as:

⟨O^⟩G=⟨ψL,G|O^|ψR,G⟩/⟨ψL,G|ψR,G⟩=limΘ→∞⟨ψL|e−Θ​H^​O^​e−Θ​H^|ψR⟩/⟨ψL|e−2​Θ​H^|ψR⟩subscriptdelimited-⟨⟩^𝑂𝐺quantum-operator-productsubscript𝜓𝐿𝐺^𝑂subscript𝜓𝑅𝐺inner-productsubscript𝜓𝐿𝐺subscript𝜓𝑅𝐺subscript→Θquantum-operator-productsubscript𝜓𝐿superscript𝑒Θ^𝐻^𝑂superscript𝑒Θ^𝐻subscript𝜓𝑅quantum-operator-productsubscript𝜓𝐿superscript𝑒2Θ^𝐻subscript𝜓𝑅\displaystyle\langle\hat{O}\rangle_{G}=\langle\psi_{L,G}|\hat{O}|\psi_{R,G}\rangle/\langle\psi_{L,G}|\psi_{R,G}\rangle=\lim_{\Theta\rightarrow\infty}\langle\psi_{L}|e^{-\Theta\hat{H}}\hat{O}e^{-\Theta\hat{H}}|\psi_{R}\rangle/\langle\psi_{L}|e^{-2\Theta\hat{H}}|\psi_{R}\rangle (6)

Consequently, we can implement the standard procedure of Trotter decomposition and Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, as employed in the conventional projector QMC algorithm for Hermitian systems, to evaluate the ground-state expectation value of the observables in non-Hermitian systems in terms of Eq. (6). Under Trotter decomposition, the projector parameter is decomposed into Nτsubscript𝑁𝜏N_{\tau} imaginary-time slices ΔτsubscriptΔ𝜏\Delta_{\tau}, where Δτ=Θ/NτsubscriptΔ𝜏Θsubscript𝑁𝜏\Delta_{\tau}=\Theta/N_{\tau}. The Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation is utilized to decouple the four-fermion interacting terms into the bilinear-fermion operators coupled to auxiliary fields.

We perform projector QMC simulations to investigate the ground-state properties of the non-Hermitian Hubbard model introduced in Eq. (LABEL:E1) the main text. In our work, we choose right (left) trial wave function as the ground-state wave function of the non-interacting part of the model H0subscript𝐻0H_{0} (H0†superscriptsubscript𝐻0†H_{0}^{\dagger}). In our simulation, we fix projector parameter Θ=2​LΘ2𝐿\Theta=2L, and have carefully checked the convergence of results against using larger values of ΘΘ\Theta. We employ the discrete H-S transformation to decouple the Hubbard interaction in non-Hermitian Hamiltonian Eq. (LABEL:E1):

e−Δτ​U2​(ni↑+ni↓)2=∑l=±1,±2γ​(l)​ei​Δτ​U2​η​(l)​(ni↑+ni↓)superscript𝑒subscriptΔ𝜏𝑈2superscriptsubscript𝑛↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑛↓𝑖absent2subscript𝑙plus-or-minus1plus-or-minus2𝛾𝑙superscript𝑒𝑖subscriptΔ𝜏𝑈2𝜂𝑙subscript𝑛↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑛↓𝑖absent\displaystyle e^{-\frac{\Delta_{\tau}U}{2}(n_{i\uparrow}+n_{i\downarrow})^{2}}=\sum_{l=\pm 1,\pm 2}\gamma(l)e^{i\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_{\tau}U}{2}}\eta(l)(n_{i\uparrow}+n_{i\downarrow})} (7)

We have verified that Δ​τΔ𝜏\Delta\tau is small enough to guarantee the convergence of results.

I.2 Section II: Sign problem free for 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetric non-Hermitian Hubbard model

In this section, we show that the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian Eq. (LABEL:E1) is 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetric, and more importantly, sign-problem-free in QMC simulation with the algorithm of generalized projector QMC for non-Hermitian systems. As shown in Eq. (LABEL:E1) of main text, the model Hamiltonian reads:

H=∑⟨i,j⟩{−(t+δ)​ci↑†​cj↑−(t−δ)​cj↑†​ci↑−(t−δ)​ci↓†​cj↓−(t+δ)​cj↓†​ci↓}+∑iU2​(ci↑†​ci↑−12)​(ci↓†​ci↓−12)𝐻subscript𝑖𝑗𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↑𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑗absentsubscript𝑐↑𝑖absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↓𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↓𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↓𝑗absentsubscript𝑐↓𝑖absentsubscript𝑖𝑈2subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↑𝑖absent12subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↓𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↓𝑖absent12\begin{split}H=\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}\{-(t+\delta)c^{\dagger}_{i\uparrow}c_{j\uparrow}-(t-\delta)c^{\dagger}_{j\uparrow}c_{i\uparrow}-(t-\delta)c^{\dagger}_{i\downarrow}c_{j\downarrow}-(t+\delta)c^{\dagger}_{j\downarrow}c_{i\downarrow}\}+\sum_{i}\frac{U}{2}(c^{\dagger}_{i\uparrow}c_{i\uparrow}-\frac{1}{2})(c^{\dagger}_{i\downarrow}c_{i\downarrow}-\frac{1}{2})\end{split} (9)

Considering spatially inversion transformation under bond center 𝒫𝒫\mathcal{P} and time reversal operation 𝒯:i​K​σy:𝒯𝑖𝐾subscript𝜎𝑦\mathcal{T}:iK\sigma_{y}, where σysubscript𝜎𝑦\sigma_{y} denotes second Pauli Matrix in spin space and K𝐾K is Hermitian conjugation. Obviously, the Hamiltonian Eq. (LABEL:E1) is invariant under 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} transformation. Thus, the model we considered is 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetric featuring many interesting properties discussed in the literatures Bender and Boettcher (1998); Rüter et al. (2010).

Under the discrete Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation defined in Eq. (7), the Hubbard interacting term is decoupled to the non-interacting operators coupled to the classical auxiliary fields depending on space and imaginary time. The decoupled Hamiltonian after H-S transformation at a given imaginary-time slice reads:

Hτ=∑⟨i,j⟩{−(t+δ)​ci↑†​cj↑−(t−δ)​cj↑†​ci↑−(t−δ)​ci↓†​cj↓−(t+δ)​cj↓†​ci↓}+i​λ​∑iΔτ​U2​η​(i,τ)​(ni↑+ni↓)subscript𝐻𝜏subscript𝑖𝑗𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↑𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑗absentsubscript𝑐↑𝑖absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↓𝑖absentsubscript𝑐↓𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↓𝑗absentsubscript𝑐↓𝑖absent𝑖𝜆subscript𝑖subscriptΔ𝜏𝑈2𝜂𝑖𝜏subscript𝑛↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑛↓𝑖absent\displaystyle H_{\tau}=\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}\{-(t+\delta)c^{\dagger}_{i\uparrow}c_{j\uparrow}-(t-\delta)c^{\dagger}_{j\uparrow}c_{i\uparrow}-(t-\delta)c^{\dagger}_{i\downarrow}c_{j\downarrow}-(t+\delta)c^{\dagger}_{j\downarrow}c_{i\downarrow}\}+i\lambda\sum_{i}\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_{\tau}U}{2}}\eta(i,\tau)(n_{i\uparrow}+n_{i\downarrow}) (10)

where ni↑(↓)=ci↑(↓)†​ci↑(↓)subscript𝑛↑𝑖↓subscriptsuperscript𝑐†↑𝑖↓subscript𝑐↑𝑖↓n_{i\uparrow(\downarrow)}=c^{\dagger}_{i\uparrow(\downarrow)}c_{i\uparrow(\downarrow)} is the electronic density operator on site i𝑖i with spin polarization in up(down)-direction. To prove the absence of sign problem, we introduce a partial particle-hole transformation as follows:

ci↑→di↑ci↓→di↓†​(−1)αiformulae-sequence→subscript𝑐↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑑↑𝑖absent→subscript𝑐↓𝑖absentsubscriptsuperscript𝑑†↓𝑖absentsuperscript1subscript𝛼𝑖\displaystyle c_{i\uparrow}\rightarrow d_{i\uparrow}\quad c_{i\downarrow}\rightarrow d^{\dagger}_{i\downarrow}(-1)^{\alpha_{i}} (11)

where αi=±1subscript𝛼𝑖plus-or-minus1\alpha_{i}=\pm 1 if the site i𝑖i belongs to A(B) sublattice. Under such transformation, the decoupled Hamiltonian Eq. (10) reads:

Hτ=∑⟨i,j⟩{−(t+δ)​di↑†​dj↑−(t−δ)​dj↑†​di↑−(t+δ)​di↓†​dj↓−(t−δ)​dj↓†​di↓}+i​λ​∑iΔτ​U2​η​(i,τ)​(ni↑−ni↓)subscript𝐻𝜏subscript𝑖𝑗𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑑†↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑑↑𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑑†↑𝑗absentsubscript𝑑↑𝑖absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑑†↓𝑖absentsubscript𝑑↓𝑗absent𝑡𝛿subscriptsuperscript𝑑†↓𝑗absentsubscript𝑑↓𝑖absent𝑖𝜆subscript𝑖subscriptΔ𝜏𝑈2𝜂𝑖𝜏subscript𝑛↑𝑖absentsubscript𝑛↓𝑖absent\displaystyle H_{\tau}=\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}\{-(t+\delta)d^{\dagger}_{i\uparrow}d_{j\uparrow}-(t-\delta)d^{\dagger}_{j\uparrow}d_{i\uparrow}-(t+\delta)d^{\dagger}_{i\downarrow}d_{j\downarrow}-(t-\delta)d^{\dagger}_{j\downarrow}d_{i\downarrow}\}+i\lambda\sum_{i}\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_{\tau}U}{2}}\eta(i,\tau)(n_{i\uparrow}-n_{i\downarrow}) (12)

which is invariant under time-reversal symmetry T=i​σy​K𝑇𝑖subscript𝜎𝑦𝐾T=i\sigma_{y}K. If the decoupled Hamiltonian under H-S transformation preserves an anti-unitary symmetry satisfying T2=−1superscript𝑇21T^{2}=-1, the model is sign-problem-free in QMC simulation. Consequently, the non-Hermitian Hubbard model considered in our study is absent from sign problem in QMC simulation.

I.3 Section III: Exact diagonalization results

It is easily shown that there exists an exact exceptional point at the δ=t𝛿𝑡\delta=t in the model LABEL:E1 in the absence of Hubbard interaction. In this section, we investigate the stability of exceptional points (EP) in the model LABEL:E1 with Hubbard interaction. The Hamiltonian LABEL:E1 preserves 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetry even in the presence of Hubabrd interaction. Nevertheless, the existence of interaction makes it infeasible to access the exceptional point straightforwardly. Hence, we perform exact diagonalization to calculate the eigenvalues of Hamiltonian LABEL:E1, and plot the distribution of eigenvalues in Fig. 5. The horizontal and vertical axis represent real and imaginary parts of eigenvalues, respectively. As shown in Fig. 5(a−cac{\rm{a-c}}), when δ≤1𝛿1\delta\leq 1, all the eigenvalues reside in the real axis, implying 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetry is not broken. Once the value of δ𝛿\delta is increased to δ>1𝛿1\delta>1, the complex eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian appear and 𝒫​𝒯𝒫𝒯\mathcal{PT} symmetry is broken (see Fig. 5.(d−fdf{\rm{d-f}}) for δ=1.05,1.1,1.2𝛿1.051.11.2\delta=1.05,1.1,1.2). We have performed the calculation in various values of U𝑈U and the conclusion still holds. Consequently, our numerical results strongly suggest the exceptional point δc=1subscript𝛿𝑐1\delta_{c}=1 is stable against Hubbard interaction in the model LABEL:E1.

I.4 Section IV: QMC results of AFM structure factor in z𝑧z-direction and x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane

The non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping reduces the spin rotational S​U​(2)𝑆𝑈2SU(2) symmetry down to a U​(1)𝑈1U(1), corresponding to spin rotational symmetry in the x−y𝑥𝑦x-y plane, leading to the consequence that AFM structure factor in z𝑧z direction SA​Fzsubscriptsuperscript𝑆𝑧𝐴𝐹S^{z}_{AF} is not equivalent to the one in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane SA​Fx​ysubscriptsuperscript𝑆𝑥𝑦𝐴𝐹S^{xy}_{AF}. In this section, we explicitly show that AFM order in x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane is dominant over the ordering in z𝑧z-direction owing to the existence of non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping. To this end, we calculate the transverse/longitudinal AFM structure factor as a function of Hubbard interaction strength U𝑈U for δ=0.4,0.6𝛿0.40.6\delta=0.4,0.6, as shown in Fig 6(a) and (b), respectively, unambiguously revealing that transverse AFM ordering is always stronger than the longitudinal one within the parameter regime under consideration, and the difference is more prominent with increasing non-Hermitian asymmetric hoppoing δ𝛿\delta. Hence, we conclude that in the presence of non-Hermitian asymmetric hopping, the x​y𝑥𝑦xy-plane AFM ordering is dominant over AFM ordering in z𝑧z-direction.

I.5 Section V: QMC results of critical properties for δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6

In the maintext, we have investigated the critical properties of the quantum phase transition between Dirac semi-metal and AFM phase for δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4, and extract the critical exponents via the standard procedure of finite-size scaling analysis. Unexpectedly, the results reveal the critical exponents of the phase transition is consistent with the Hermitian chiral XY universality class within errorbars. In this section, we present the results of critical properties of DSM to NHAFM transition for δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6, confirming the conclusion of emergent Hermitian chiral XY universality class from the non-Hermitian lattice model.

Fixing δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6, we present the results of data collapse analysis for AFM structure factor and AFM correlation-length ratio in Fig. 7(a) and Fig. 7(b), respectively. Fig. 7(a) is the results of scaled AFM structure factors L1+η​SA​FX​Ysuperscript𝐿1𝜂superscriptsubscript𝑆𝐴𝐹𝑋𝑌L^{1+\eta}S_{AF}^{XY} as a function of (U/Uc−1)​L1/ν𝑈subscript𝑈𝑐1superscript𝐿1𝜈(U/U_{c}-1)L^{1/\nu} for different linear system sizes L=15,18,21,24𝐿15182124L=15,18,21,24. Given the critical exponents obtained from the analysis for the results of δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4, the scaled AFM structure factors for different system sizes collapse to a single smooth curve as a function of (U/Uc−1)​L1/ν𝑈subscript𝑈𝑐1superscript𝐿1𝜈(U/U_{c}-1)L^{1/\nu}, indicating the DSM-NHAFM quantum phase transition for δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6 belongs to the same universality class with δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4, namely chiral-XY universality class. The same procedure of analysis is performed for correlation-length ratio. The results of correlation-length ratios for different linear system sizes obeys the scaling function with the choice of critical exponents. We also perform long-log plot of AFM structure factors versus linear system size L𝐿L at the quantum critical point Uc=3.08subscript𝑈𝑐3.08U_{c}=3.08, and the anomalous dimension η=0.6146𝜂0.6146\eta=0.6146 is given by the linear fitting, which is consistent with η=0.603±0.03𝜂plus-or-minus0.6030.03\eta=0.603\pm 0.03 for δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4 with error bar. Consequently, the phase transition from DSM to NHAFM phase for δ=0.6𝛿0.6\delta=0.6 and δ=0.4𝛿0.4\delta=0.4 belong to the same universality classes consisent with chiral XY transition, suggesting the emergent Hermiticity at the QCP between DSM and NHAFM phase in model Eq. (LABEL:E1).
